claim: Future economies will be increasingly plant-based.
source: With growing populations and pressing environmental problems, future economies will be increasingly plant-based.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future economic trends based on current population and environmental pressures.

claim: The relationship between sequence, structure and function of a protein has been explored from many angles, from biophysics to drug discovery.
source: The relationship between the sequence, structure and function of a protein has been explored from many angles, from biophysics to drug discovery (Brausemann et al., 2017; Rajendran et al., 2018; Shang et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research.

claim: The structure-to-function paradigm has driven the development of innovative technologies in imaging, mass spectrometry, genomics and bioinformatics.
source: This long-standing paradigm has driven the development of innovative technologies in imaging, mass spectrometry, genomics and bioinformatics (Camp et al., 2019; Mallis et al., 2020; Nakane et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research.

claim: The location of molecules is essential for their function at all scales, from molecular complexes to cells, organs, organisms and whole communities.
source: Yet an evolving paradigm stating that the location of molecules is essential for their function at all scales, from molecular complexes to cells, organs, organisms and whole communities, also holds true (Figure 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 1 which illustrates examples at different scales.

claim: Functions of protein complexes can be determined by their localization in membrane microdomains.
source: At the molecular level, functions of protein complexes can be determined by their localization in membrane microdomains (Jarsch et al., 2014) or by dynamic protein interactions (Obata, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: Multi-enzyme complexes work as molecular machines to channel intermediate metabolites and produce specific molecular products in a highly controlled manner.
source: At the molecular level, compelling examples of the location-to-function paradigm include the multi-enzyme complexes that work as molecular machines (so-called 'metabolons') to channel intermediate metabolites and produce specific molecular products in a highly controlled manner (Obata, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: The partitioning of proteins and lipids into organelles plays crucial roles in molecular trafficking and signal transduction.
source: At the cellular level, the partitioning of proteins and lipids into organelles – and even membrane microdomains within organelles – plays crucial roles in molecular trafficking and signal transduction, which have great impacts in many biological processes such as plant development and defence responses (Jarsch et al., 2014; Xing et al., 2019; Yu et al., 2020; Heinze et al., 2020; Shimizu et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published research.

claim: Protein function can be dynamically regulated by a change in location, such as the activation of transcription factors by translocation into the nucleus.
source: Protein function can also be dynamically regulated by a change in location, such as the activation of transcription factors by translocation into the nucleus (Jiang et al., 2020; Marchive et al., 2013; Ramon et al., 2019; Pastor-Cantizano et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published research.

claim: C4 photosynthesis is an example of how differential molecular localization between cell types enhances plant performance.
source: At the tissue level, C4 photosynthesis is a classic example of how differential molecular localization between cell types enhances plant performance: differential expression of enzymes in bundle sheath and mesophyll cells in C4 plants can concentrate CO2 in close proximity to Rubisco, which is not possible in C3 plants where the enzymes are present, but not differentially expressed between the cells (Schlüter and Weber, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: The success of molecular approaches for crop improvement depends on a detailed understanding of the spatio-temporal regulation of genes and proteins and the production of metabolites.
source: One particular area of potential success is agriculture, as the success of molecular approaches for crop improvement depends on a detailed understanding of the spatio-temporal regulation of genes and proteins and the production of metabolites (see Wang et al., 2008 for an example of how controlling the location of gene expression impacts rice grain size and yield).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to an example in published research.

claim: Engineered early expression of WRINKLED1 during maturation increased Arabidopsis seed size and oil content.
source: For instance, engineered early expression of WRINKLED1 (WRI1, an AP2 class transcription factor) during maturation increased Arabidopsis seed size and oil content (Kanai et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Over 400 scientists participated in the first series of PCA workshops, of which 70% were early-career researchers, and 33% non-US based.
source: Over 400 scientists participated, of which 70% were early-career researchers, and 33% non-US based (Rice et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a published report.

claim: The PCA will be critical in harnessing the power of single-cell data by establishing and promoting community-supported best practices in sample preparation, data generation, analysis and integration.
source: The PCA will be critical in harnessing the power of single-cell data by establishing and promoting community-supported best practices in sample preparation, data generation, analysis and integration – including data benchmarking platforms, evaluation metrics and reference cell maps for major organ/cell types in model species.
evidence: This is a statement about the intended role and goals of the PCA initiative.

claim: The PCA efforts include integration of not only single-cell omics data, but also spatiotemporal dynamics of single cells and their connection to cell types and developmental trajectories.
source: The PCA efforts include integration of not only single-cell omics data, but also spatiotemporal dynamics of single cells and their connection to cell types and developmental trajectories.
evidence: This is a statement about the scope of the PCA initiative.

claim: The mouse brain and adult mouse cell atlases are models for comprehensive coverage and community accessibility.
source: Among the animal whole organism atlases (Lähnemann et al., 2020), the mouse brain and adult mouse cell atlases are models for comprehensive coverage and community accessibility (Rosenberg et al., 2018; Saunders et al., 2018; Zeisel et al., 2018; Tabula Muris Consortium, 2018; Han et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published research.

claim: The Human Cell Atlas' data portal includes data from 55 organs and 12 million cells.
source: The Human Cell Atlas' data portal already includes data from 55 organs and 12 million cells, and it is becoming a model for making community-generated single-cell data available at a single portal, along with APIs and data analysis pipelines made easily accessible.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the current state of the Human Cell Atlas data portal.

claim: EMBL-EBI's Single Cell Expression Atlas recently started hosting plant single-cell transcriptome data.
source: For plants, response to the environment would serve as an analogous level to behavior. EMBL-EBI's Single Cell Expression Atlas recently started hosting plant single-cell transcriptome data, which is an exciting development (Papatheodorou et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: The PCA will be developed, maintained and used by a global community with diverse scientific, technical, creative and educational backgrounds.
source: The PCA will be developed, maintained and used by a global community with diverse scientific, technical, creative and educational backgrounds (Figure 4).
evidence: This is a statement about the intended composition of the PCA community.

claim: Robust computational infrastructure development will be essential to support the research, community-building and outreach activities of the PCA.
source: Robust computational infrastructure development will be essential to support the research, community-building and outreach activities of the PCA (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a statement about the requirements for the PCA initiative.

claim: Plant cells have rigid cell walls, making some tissues and many species recalcitrant to digestion.
source: A major challenge is dissociating plant cells: due to their rigid cell walls, some tissues and many species are recalcitrant to digestion (Himmel et al., 2007; Yoo et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Single-nucleus profiling avoids the need for cell wall digestion.
source: One emerging approach that has the potential to address this issue in plants is single-nucleus profiling, which avoids the need for cell wall digestion (Giacomello, 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Nuclear isolation methods have shown promise for plant single-cell profiling.
source: Such nuclear isolation methods have already shown promise (Farmer et al., 2021; Marand et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Proximity labeling approaches bypass the need for isolating cells or organelles by tagging proteins and RNAs near a target protein in living cells and organisms.
source: Recently developed proximity labeling approaches bypass the need for isolating cells or organelles by tagging proteins and RNAs near a target protein in living cells and organisms. These methods can profile components of protein complexes, dynamic protein-protein interactions, specific cell types and subcellular locations of proteins or RNAs (Zhang et al., 2019a; Mair et al., 2019; Huang et al., 2020; Kim et al., 2019; Wang et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published research.

claim: Plants have a well-known capacity for duplication at many scales, ranging from single gene to whole genome.
source: Plants have a well-known capacity for duplication at many scales, ranging from single gene to whole genome.
evidence: This is a statement based on established scientific knowledge about plant genomes.

claim: Establishing experimental and analytical standards was key to the success of the Encyclopedia of DNA Elements project.
source: Establishing a vetted and community-approved set of experimental and analytical standards will be important. Such an approach was key to the success of the Encyclopedia of DNA Elements project, which ensured that data from multiple international laboratories were easily compared and integrated (ENCODE Project Consortium, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: The 1001 Arabidopsis Genomes website provided a user-friendly interface to download all sequencing data and was complemented with an interactive tool to explore phenotypes.
source: Likewise, the 1001 Arabidopsis Genomes website provided a user-friendly interface to download all sequencing data as phases were completed – allowing the community to begin analyses and discoveries even before publication – and was complemented with an interactive tool to explore phenotypes (Seren et al., 2016) and their genomic associations (Togninalli et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research.

claim: A typical plant has about 100 cell types.
source: A typical plant has about 100 cell types (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols/ontologies/po; Ilic et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research and a reference to an ontology database.

claim: Over 70% of applied research and development in the US is funded by industry.
source: Over 70% of applied research and development in the US is funded by industry (Khan et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Biomass is projected to be a major source of primary energy by 2050.
source: Biomass is projected to be a major source of primary energy by 2050 (Reid et al., 2020), plant-based meat and dairy products are already transforming the food industry (Shepon et al., 2018), and plant-based vaccines against several diseases are increasingly being researched (reviewed by Shahid and Daniell, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Plant-based meat and dairy products are transforming the food industry.
source: Biomass is projected to be a major source of primary energy by 2050 (Reid et al., 2020), plant-based meat and dairy products are already transforming the food industry (Shepon et al., 2018), and plant-based vaccines against several diseases are increasingly being researched (reviewed by Shahid and Daniell, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Plant-based vaccines against several diseases are increasingly being researched.
source: Biomass is projected to be a major source of primary energy by 2050 (Reid et al., 2020), plant-based meat and dairy products are already transforming the food industry (Shepon et al., 2018), and plant-based vaccines against several diseases are increasingly being researched (reviewed by Shahid and Daniell, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a review article.

claim: Recombinant DNA technology enabled the development and deployment of mRNA and DNA-based viral vaccines in 2020.
source: Two decades after this statement, in 2020, recombinant DNA technology ushered in the beginning of an end to a global pandemic that cost millions of lives, through a record-breaking runtime of development and deployment of mRNA and DNA-based viral vaccines.
evidence: This is a statement based on known events regarding COVID-19 vaccine development.

claim: Plant science constitutes a minority of life sciences in terms of funding and workforce.
source: Today, plant science constitutes a minority of life sciences in terms of funding and workforce.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of plant science funding and workforce.

claim: The differential location of a single molecule can determine one of several alternative functions.
source: The differential location of a single molecule can determine one of several alternative functions (see, for example, Smirnoff and Arnaud, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Protein translocation to different cellular domains results in different functional outcomes.
source: Furthermore, protein translocation to different cellular domains results in different functional outcomes (see for instance, Kim et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Controlling the location of gene expression impacts rice grain size and yield.
source: The success of molecular approaches for crop improvement depends on a detailed understanding of the spatio-temporal regulation of genes and proteins and the production of metabolites (see Wang et al., 2008 for an example of how controlling the location of gene expression impacts rice grain size and yield).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Spatially- or cell-type-resolved expression data are missing or incomplete for most crop plants.
source: Currently, these spatially- or cell-type-resolved expression data are missing or incomplete for most crop plants and there is no centralized repository for their integration.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of data availability for crop plants.

claim: There is no centralized repository for integration of spatially- or cell-type-resolved expression data for crop plants.
source: Currently, these spatially- or cell-type-resolved expression data are missing or incomplete for most crop plants and there is no centralized repository for their integration.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of data infrastructure for crop plants.

claim: Three workshops were held virtually during May and June of 2020.
source: Three workshops were held virtually during May and June of 2020.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the timing of the workshops.

claim: Two technology-oriented workshops on single-cell sequencing and spatial proteomics and a career planning workshop were held virtually in 2021, respectively attracting 273, 253 and 42 participants.
source: Following the success of the inaugural meeting, two technology-oriented workshops on single-cell sequencing and spatial proteomics and a career planning workshop were held virtually in 2021, respectively attracting 273, 253 and 42 participants.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the workshops and their attendance.

claim: Single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq technologies make some PCA goals realistic to accomplish quickly.
source: Some of these goals can be accomplished quickly, as already existing technologies such as single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq make them realistic.
evidence: This is an inference based on the availability of existing technologies.

claim: The PCA will be critical in harnessing the power of single-cell data by establishing community-supported best practices.
source: The PCA will be critical in harnessing the power of single-cell data by establishing and promoting community-supported best practices in sample preparation, data generation, analysis and integration – including data benchmarking platforms, evaluation metrics and reference cell maps for major organ/cell types in model species.
evidence: This is a statement about the intended role of the PCA initiative.

claim: Standards for plant phenotypic data have been produced.
source: Similar standards have been produced for instance for plant phenotypic data (Papoutsoglou et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: The PCA efforts facilitate a comprehensive understanding of how different complex tissues and organs are formed during plant growth and development.
source: It therefore facilitates a comprehensive understanding of how different complex tissues and organs are formed during plant growth and development.
evidence: This is a statement about the intended outcome of the PCA initiative.

claim: Growing skepticism about science will impair the ability to aid society with the power of plant research.
source: Without these efforts, we fear that growing skepticism about science will impair the ability to aid society with the power of plant research, as apparent in the non-evidence-based regulation of gene editing in the European Union (Jorasch, 2020; Ruffell, 2018; Zimny et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by citations to published research about gene editing regulation.

claim: The OpenWorm project provides an example for modeling, visualizing and simulating various aspects of the biology and behavior of an organism.
source: In addition, the OpenWorm project provides an excellent example for modeling, visualizing and simulating various aspects of the biology and behavior of an organism (Szigeti et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: The Global Natural Product Social Molecular Networking initiative provides a model for a one-stop-shop web infrastructure to enable data generation, integration, analysis and publication from mass spectrometry.
source: Finally, the Global Natural Product Social Molecular Networking initiative provides a model for a one-stop-shop web infrastructure to enable data generation, integration, analysis and publication from mass spectrometry (Wang et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: The success of the PCA will hinge on an open and frequent dialogue between developers and users, with facilitation and guidance from a steering group.
source: The participants in the PCA Research Coordination Network anticipate that the success of the PCA will hinge on an open and frequent dialogue between developers and users, with facilitation and guidance from a steering group.
evidence: This is a statement about the anticipated requirements for PCA success.

claim: Recruiting scientists from diverse disciplines as well as from different career stages will be crucial in the successful development of the PCA.
source: Recruiting scientists from diverse disciplines as well as from different career stages will be crucial in the successful development of the PCA.
evidence: This is a statement about the requirements for PCA development.

claim: The PCA infrastructure should have a seamless integration of multi-omics data with localization data at multiple scales of the plant.
source: We envision the PCA infrastructure (that is, the technologies, standards and computational platforms used by developers to build a framework to house and make available the PCA-relevant data) to have a seamless integration of multi-omics data with localization data at multiple scales of the plant.
evidence: This is a statement about the envisioned design of the PCA infrastructure.

claim: The DREAM challenges group could be leveraged for developing data analysis, visualization and access tools.
source: For example, the DREAM challenges group could be leveraged for developing data analysis, visualization and access tools (Pham et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a suggestion supported by a citation to published research.

claim: The PCA should make efforts to liaison with data repositories, knowledge bases and data analysis hubs.
source: The PCA should make efforts to liaison with data repositories, knowledge bases and data analysis hubs such as ATTED, eFP Browser, ePlant, Ensembl Plants, Gramene, MaizeGDB, TAIR, The 1001 Arabidopsis Genomes phenotype database, NCBI's GEO, EMBL-EBI's Expression Atlas, AraPheno and others (Obayashi et al., 2007; Sullivan et al., 2019; Howe et al., 2020; Tello-Ruiz et al., 2021; Portwood, 2018; Berardini et al., 2015; Seren et al., 2016; Barrett et al., 2005; Papatheodorou et al., 2020; Waese et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a recommendation supported by citations to existing resources.

claim: OMERO is a global consortium effort aiming to standardize biological imaging data.
source: For example, OMERO is a global consortium effort aiming to standardize biological imaging data, which includes data depository as well as image processing software to translate image files into a universal format.
evidence: This is a statement about an existing consortium based on established knowledge.

claim: The PCA needs to position itself at the frontier of plant biology, looking out for emerging findings and technologies.
source: As such, the PCA needs to position itself and its community at the frontier of plant biology, looking out for emerging findings and technologies.
evidence: This is a statement about the strategic positioning of the PCA initiative.

claim: Plant meristems are multicellular machines that continually produce new cells that must be specified to fate and then guided through phases of maturation.
source: In post-embryonic development, plant meristems are remarkable multicellular machines, continually producing new cells that must be specified to fate and then guided through phases of maturation (Esau, 1953; Sinnott, 1960).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Plants present a contrast to mammalian systems with respect to the plasticity they maintain.
source: Furthermore, plants present a fascinating contrast to mammalian systems with respect to the plasticity they maintain (Borges, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Perennial plants show meristematic plasticity, where only a subset of meristems per season are activated.
source: For example, perennial plants often show meristematic plasticity, where only a subset of meristems per season are activated, and with the meristematic activity frequently modulated in response to external and internal cues (Tylewicz et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: The threat of invasion of foreign biota into cellular and intercellular spaces often induces localized hypersensitive responses of programmed cell death.
source: An example can be found in how the threat of invasion of foreign biota into cellular and intercellular spaces often induces localized hypersensitive responses of programmed cell death (Jones and Dangl, 2006; Ngou et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Infection by the symbiont through the root hairs takes place asynchronously in nitrogen-fixing symbioses.
source: In the latter case, infection by the symbiont through the root hairs takes place asynchronously, so bulk sampling often leads to profiles that are a heterogeneous mixture of cell states (Libault et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Plants have evolved many new specialized cell types, allowing adaptation to new ecological niches.
source: From rhizoids to pollen, plants have evolved many new specialized cell types, allowing adaptation to new ecological niches.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge of plant evolution.

claim: Specific cell types in the root harbor molecular mechanisms to perceive and respond to environmental stimuli, suggesting they may act as 'gatekeepers' for these responses.
source: In addition, specific cell types in the root harbor molecular mechanisms to perceive and respond to environmental stimuli, suggesting they may act as 'gatekeepers' for these responses (Henderson and Gilliham, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Previous attempts to use expression patterns of homologous genes in distantly related species to assess functional orthology have provided insights.
source: Previous attempts to use expression patterns of homologous genes in distantly related species to assess functional orthology have provided insights (Adamski et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Bulk tissues collected in different species may have substantially different composition of cell types.
source: However, bulk tissues collected in different species may have substantially different composition of cell types (Huang and Schiefelbein, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: The presence of novel cell types in some species may be obscured in whole organ samples.
source: Furthermore, the presence of novel cell types in some species may be obscured in whole organ samples (Kajala et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Untargeted spatial transcriptomic methods have the potential for the resolution and throughput needed for mapping cells back to their tissue location.
source: In particular, untargeted methods (that is, methods based on unbiased sequencing rather than hybridization of a limited set of predefined probes) have the potential for the resolution and throughput needed (Giacomello et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: The hierarchical approach proposed by the common coordinate framework for humans can serve as a starting point for plant nomenclature systems.
source: The hierarchical approach proposed by the common coordinate framework for humans can serve as a starting point (Rood et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Advancement in sequence alignment methods, such as incorporating structural information, could help to discover distant homologs.
source: Advancement in sequence alignment methods, such as incorporating structural information, could help to discover these distant homologs (Morton et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: It is routine to deposit next-generation sequencing, processed expression data, proteomics, metabolomics and protein structures in numerous repositories worldwide.
source: For example, it is now routine to deposit next-generation sequencing, processed expression data, proteomics, metabolomics and protein structures in numerous repositories worldwide (Deutsch et al., 2017; Kaminuma et al., 2010; Leinonen et al., 2011; NCBI Resource Coordinators, 2018; wwPDB consortium, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research.

claim: A combination of automated searches and manual curation of datasets from existing data repositories can be used to build the PCA data infrastructure.
source: A combination of automated searches and manual curation of datasets from existing data repositories can be used to build the PCA data infrastructure.
evidence: This is a statement about the proposed approach for building the PCA infrastructure.

claim: Reference genome databases provide gene and pathway annotation resources.
source: Reference genome databases such as TAIR, Phytozome, Gramene, EnsemblPlants and others that provide gene and pathway annotation resources (e.g. Gene Ontology) could enable an initial assessment of gene structure, location and function (Berardini et al., 2015; Goodstein et al., 2012; Howe et al., 2020; Tello-Ruiz et al., 2021; The Gene Ontology Consortium, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published resources.

claim: Single-cell datasets should be made available in both raw and processed data formats and linked from the public-facing PCA website.
source: To this end, single-cell datasets should be made available in both raw and processed data formats and linked from the public-facing PCA website.
evidence: This is a recommendation for the PCA infrastructure.

claim: The PCA portal should include web-based tools to generate, access and query relevant data and metadata using a standardized ontology for metadata.
source: In addition to providing links to data repositories, the PCA portal should include web-based tools to generate, access and query relevant data and metadata using a standardized ontology for metadata, similar to the Single Cell Expression Atlas (Papatheodorou et al., 2020) and the Human Cell Atlas implementation of metadata types.
evidence: This is a recommendation supported by citations to existing resources.

claim: Multiscale networks can provide an intuitive method to discretize and integrate different data types.
source: Multiscale networks can provide an intuitive method to discretize and integrate different data types (Duran-Nebreda and Bassel, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Methods for data standardization and curation will be critical tools to mitigate challenges with existing data.
source: In addition, methods for data standardization and curation will be critical tools to mitigate challenges with existing data, create best practices for collecting new data and ensure consistency to allow for data exchange and interoperability (Sansone et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Existing solutions and concepts of cell type ontologies are broadly applied in vertebrates and are available for plants.
source: Existing solutions and concepts of such ontologies are broadly applied in vertebrates and are available for plants, though they need to be widely adopted by the PCA community (Avraham et al., 2008; Bard et al., 2005 ; Diehl et al., 2016; Ilic et al., 2007; Xia and Yanai, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research.

claim: The PCA vision is different from the Human Cell Atlas in that it embraces cell atlas data from a diverse array of plants rather than a single organism.
source: The Human Cell Atlas is for a single organism with over 200 cell types, whereas the PCA community embraces cell atlas data from a diverse array of plants.
evidence: This is a comparison between the PCA and Human Cell Atlas initiatives.

claim: The PCA is an essential step towards realizing the vision of a Transparent Plant.
source: The PCA is an essential step towards realizing the vision of a Transparent Plant, a simulated environment where virtual plants can be built from parts and behaviors (Henkhaus et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: The Virtual Plant database is an essential component of the PCA vision and infrastructure.
source: Finally, we see the Virtual Plant database (Katari et al., 2010) as an essential component of the PCA vision and infrastructure.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Programs that facilitate collaboration across borders will be valuable in advancing the goals of the PCA initiative.
source: As the PCA has an international reach, programs that facilitate collaboration across borders will be valuable in advancing the goals of the initiative, such as partnering programs by the Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council (BBSRC) in the United Kingdom, European Commission's Horizon Europe and the United States' Fulbright scholars program.
evidence: This is a statement about potential funding and collaboration mechanisms.

claim: Government funding for basic research has been steadily decreasing.
source: While governments are the major sources of funding for basic research, their level of funding has been steadily decreasing (Khan et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Foundations are the major source of private basic research funding.
source: Foundations are the major source of private basic research funding and are less constrained by time, politics and topic.
evidence: This is a statement about research funding sources.

claim: The Chan Zuckerberg Initiative provided substantial funds to develop technologies for the Human Cell Atlas initiative.
source: One of their success stories is the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative providing substantial funds to develop technologies for the Human Cell Atlas initiative.
evidence: This is a statement about a known funding example.

claim: A thorough understanding of plant systems is essential for designing effective agro-biotech solutions.
source: A thorough understanding of plant systems is essential for designing effective agro-biotech solutions leading to new crop varieties, and to innovative crop protection products that can leverage sustainable food production.
evidence: This is a statement based on inference about the requirements for agricultural biotechnology.

claim: In 2004, John Avise wrote that the ultimate contribution of recombinant DNA techniques to the broader human enterprise remained uncertain.
source: In 2004, the evolutionary biologist John Avise wrote that ''despite nearly three decades of experience with recombinant DNA techniques, the ultimate contribution to the broader human enterprise remains uncertain'' (Avise, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.
